title: Bisect strata overlay procedure for trace-sampled canary comparisons
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a practical procedure for diagnosing subtle performance regressions discovered via alerts or canary deltas where single-number metrics (p50/p95) point to a regression but root cause is unclear. The workflow combines sampled span overlays (trace-level diffs), stratified bisecting across rollout dimensions (code, model, quantization, kernel), and targeted micro-profiling on candidate commits or model variants. The goal is to minimize time-to-root-cause while producing artifacts suitable for postmortem and automated detection rules.

When to use this doc:
- Canary shows a small-but-consistent p95 increase after a rollout.
- Alerts fire but initial dashboards don't isolate a single service/component.
- Regression reproduces intermittently and is correlated with specific traffic slices (long prompts, embeddings, function-calls).

Quick checklist (first 20 minutes):
1) Snapshot the alert: capture time range, affected routes, model id, and canary tag.
2) Pull the canary vs baseline aggregate metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, error-rate, tail-token throughput, token-cost deltas.
   - Grafana panels: serving_runtime.latency_histogram, route.token_throughput, model.kv_cache_hit_rate.
3) Collect 200–500 sampled traces from both canary and baseline windows (balanced by route and prompt length).
4) Create a light-weight overlay diff of spans (see Overlay method below).
5) If the diff points to a subsystem (e.g., tokenizer, kernel-compile, KV cache refill), trigger targeted bisect.

Trace overlay method (span-diff basics):
- Sample selection: prefer traces with similar high-level shape (same route, same sequence-length bucket ±10%). Choose N=250 per side when possible.
- Normalization: map spans by semantic name and relative ordering rather than absolute timestamps. Collapse repeated child spans into median duration buckets (reduces noise from tokenization loops).
- Overlay visualization: produce a CSV with columns: span_key, median_baseline_ms, median_canary_ms, p90_baseline_ms, p90_canary_ms, sample_count. Use small bar chart overlays in Grafana or QuickPlot to highlight spans with >15% relative increase and absolute delta >2 ms.
- Heuristics to trust a span delta: delta persists across at least two different prompt-length strata OR the span accounts for >=15% of end-to-end p95 in canary window.

Stratified bisect plan (why strata matters):
Often regressions are not uniform across all traffic. Bisecting across a single commit range is slow if the root cause only affects long sequences or embeddings. Instead, run parallel bisects across orthogonal strata:
- Code commit range (git bisect): kernel/ops changes, runtime scheduling, batching logic.
- Model variant/version: tokenizer changes, model architecture, attention kernel layout.
- Quantization/profile: different int8/4/optimizations.
- Hardware/kernel selection: cuBLAS vs CUTLASS path, custom fused kernels.
- Traffic slice: short prompts (<64 tokens), medium (64–512), long (>512), streaming vs non-streaming.

Recommended bisect workflow:
1) Start a shallow verification: run a minimal synthetic harness replaying representative requests for the suspicious stratum (e.g., 100 long prompts). If you can reproduce the delta locally, proceed to bisect.
2) Parallelize: spawn multiple small bisect jobs concurrently, each constrained to a single stratum. Each job runs an automated harness that compares a candidate commit/variant against baseline and reports p95/p99 deltas plus span-overlay summary.
3) Accept/reject threshold: a job flags a commit as suspect if it reproduces >=10% relative p95 regression AND the overlay shows a consistent span delta by the heuristics above.
4) Narrow to 1–3 commits/changes for focused profiling.

Micro-profiling checklist (once suspects isolated):
- Attach sampling profiler (e.g., Nsight Systems or per-process eBPF stacks): collect 60–120s of representative traffic.
- Kernel-level counters: GPU SM utilization, PCIe stalls, kernel-launch times, and memory-copy peaks.
- Runtime metrics: batch sizes, queueing_delay_ms, kv_cache_miss_rate, token-fanout.
- Hot-spot capture: record top-20 Python/C++ call stacks and kernel names sorted by self-time and cumulative time.
- Compare symbol-level stacks across baseline/canary to find changed call paths or newly introduced locks/contended queues.

Common root causes we've seen and quick indicators:
- Tokenization overhead spike: overlay shows tokenizer.decode spans ballooning on long prompts. Check tokenizer parallelism and caching.
- KV cache refill storms: p95 jumps on long-streamed sessions with repeated cache-prefetch spans. Indicators: kv_cache_hit_rate drop and high memory-copy rates.
- New kernel fallback: overlay shows a short sequence of kernel-compile or compatibility wrapper spans increasing. Check kernel selection logs and op attributes.
- Scheduling regression: queueing_delay_ms increases while raw GPU utilization drops. Look for priority inversion or batch-merging changes.
- Quantization mismatch: heavy branch in runtime executing dequant-reshape spans more frequently. Check quantization config flags.

Rollout/canary comparison mechanics:
- Canary windows: use 30–60 minute windows with stable traffic; sample evenly across minutes.
- Baseline: the stable pool immediately preceding the canary rollout (avoid windows with infra noise like autoscaler events).
- Compare both raw aggregates and token-normalized metrics (latency per token for streaming).
- Produce artifact package: overlay CSV, raw trace bundles (ddtrace/jaeger files), profiler captures, and a 1-page executive summary with root cause hypothesis and confidence level (low/medium/high).

Automation & tooling tips:
- Bisect jobs should be scripted: given a commit or model id, the job runs the harness, uploads traces to storage, runs overlay script, and returns a single verdict JSON (fields: commit, stratum, p95_delta_pct, overlay_top_span).
- Use lightweight SQLite result store for concurrent jobs to avoid race conditions in CI.
- Add an automated daily job that replays a small fixed prompt set across the latest tip and baseline to detect regressions early (smoke-bisect).

Acceptance and rollback guidance:
- If root cause confirmed and regression >=20% p95 across >=2 strata: immediate rollback to baseline while follow-up fix is gated.
- If regression is narrow (single stratum, low user impact): hold rollout and create a mitigations plan (patch or config toggle).
- For ambiguous cases: flag release as "investigate-more" and reduce canary traffic to 5% with additional tracing enabled.

Postmortem artifacts (minimum):
- Timeline of detection -> triage -> bisect -> fix/rollback with timestamps.
- Artifact bundle link (traces, overlays, profiler captures).
- Root cause summary and line-level pointers (PRs, commits).
- Follow-up items: monitoring rule changes, regression unit-tests, rollout checklist updates.

Examples (commands and queries):
- Grafana PromQL example to compare p95: 100 * (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(serving_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)))
- Quick overlay generation (pseudo): python tools/overlay.py --baseline traces/baseline/*.json --canary traces/canary/*.json --out overlays/canary-vs-baseline.csv --top 30
- Start a bisect job: ./tools/bisect-run.sh --commits=a1b2..d4e5 --stratum=long-prompts --harness=tests/replay_long_prompts.yaml

Notes and heuristics:
- Avoid being misled by aggregate p95 changes driven by a tiny volume of heavy requests. Always normalize by request volume per stratum.
- Do not disable sampling or reduce tracing depth during bisect — the overlays rely on consistent instrumentation.
- Prefer median-of-median comparisons across multiple small windows rather than a single large aggregate which can be skewed by outliers.

Contact and escalation:
- Primary owner: Maya Chen (pager: @mchen).
- Escalation: Eng SRE on-call -> Serving Runtime lead (Diego) -> Platform infra if GPU/kernel implicated.

Revision history:
- 2025-01-10 initial draft (Maya Chen)
- 2025-01-16 added parallel strata bisect guidance (Rhea Patel)
- 2025-01-22 included profiler checklist and acceptance thresholds (Owen Li)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add canned Grafana panels and a lightweight UI to kick off stratified bisects from the alert dashboard.
- Define exact statistical test for "consistent span delta" (bootstrap vs t-test) and automate verdicts.

Bottom line: this procedure trades some upfront engineering (overlay tooling, scripted bisects) for a much faster and less noisy path to root cause when canaries and alerts surface fuzzy regressions. Follow the strata-first approach: split the universe of traffic, bisect in parallel, and use span overlays to focus heavy-weight profiling only where it matters.
